# Results — Study 475 (DeMarker)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **the DeMarker
exhausts and reverses at extremes: a reading rising out of oversold (<0.3) bounces up** — encoded
as a mechanical rule. The DeMarker (DeMark, period 14) is built from the highs and lows
(DeMax = max(ΔHigh,0), DeMin = max(−ΔLow,0), DeMarker = SMA(DeMax)/(SMA(DeMax)+SMA(DeMin))); a long
fires the first bar the DeMarker turns **up** out of the <0.3 zone, entered at the **next close**
(one documented lag), and we measure the forward 5/10/20/60-day return. Offline & deterministic
once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **1167** mechanical DeMarker oversold-rising turns pooled across the 5 tapes (period = 14, oversold = 0.30) |
| Timing / costs | DeMarker uses bars through *t* only; trigger read on close of *t*; enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per entry |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid ETFs; this is a
> single-instrument timing study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so survivorship affects only the
> drift baseline (which is exactly what the random-entry control neutralizes).

## The signal — DeMarker oversold-rising vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch entry-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = entry − random.

| horizon | n | entry | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (entry−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 1166 | +43.5 bps  | 62% | +4.98 | +34.5 bps  | **+9.0 bps**  | +41.5 bps  | +0.76 | 0.448 |
| 10-day | 1166 | +96.7 bps  | 63% | +7.00 | +71.4 bps  | **+25.3 bps** | +94.7 bps  | +1.60 | 0.110 |
| 20-day | 1164 | +182.1 bps | 67% | +7.66 | +126.3 bps | **+55.8 bps** | +180.1 bps | **+2.61** | **0.009** |
| 60-day | 1137 | +397.9 bps | 69% | +7.78 | +334.8 bps | **+63.1 bps** | +395.9 bps | +1.80 | 0.072 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks spectacular (**+7.66** at 20 days) — but
most of that is **beta**: long-only entries on an upward-drifting index inherit the drift. Against
the **drift-matched random baseline**, the DeMarker entry beats the dart by a positive but small
margin at *every* horizon, and the difference **clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar at exactly one
horizon** (20-day Welch *t* = +2.61, *p* = 0.009); at 5/10/60 days it is +0.76/+1.60/+1.80, never
significant. So there is *some* signal — more than the usual technical-indicator mirage — but it is
not robust across horizons.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — positive everywhere, but one name carries it

| ticker | entries | entry | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (entry−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 225 | +165.8 bps | +3.12 | +155.8 bps | **+10.0 bps** |
| QQQ | 224 | +199.2 bps | +3.11 | +173.4 bps | **+25.7 bps** |
| IWM | 249 | +206.9 bps | +3.70 | +61.4 bps  | **+145.5 bps** |
| DIA | 213 | +198.2 bps | +4.33 | +147.3 bps | **+50.9 bps** |
| GLD | 256 | +143.3 bps | +4.02 | +104.8 bps | **+38.5 bps** |

The delta is positive in **all 5** names — encouraging — but it is wildly concentrated in **IWM**
(small-caps, +145.5 bps), where the random baseline is anomalously weak. **Drop IWM and the pooled
20-day Welch *t* falls from +2.61 to +1.40 (*p* = 0.162)** — i.e. the only significant horizon is
carried by a single instrument. That fragility is the verdict's hinge.

## Timing placebo — phase-scramble the oscillator

The decisive "does the DeMarker's *timing* matter?" test: rebuild the oscillator from a circular
**rotation** of the DeMax/DeMin streams, preserving the oscillator's exact marginal but breaking
its alignment with price, then fire the same oversold-rising rule. If the timing carries
information, the real result sits in the right tail.

| test | observed 20d entry return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY phase-scramble DeMarker | +165.8 bps | **0.044** | 500 |

The real DeMarker beats **95.6%** of phase-scrambled oscillators (*p* = 0.044) — it *just* clears
0.05, so the timing is **marginally** load-bearing rather than pure nonsense. Combined with the
single-horizon, single-ticker significance, this is a "Mixed" rather than an outright "Busted".

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real exhaustion bounce

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* rebound keyed to the oversold-rising trigger (knob
`edge`), the same rule behaves exactly as it must — so the fragile real-tape result is honestly
measured, not a dead (or trigger-happy) detector.

| planted edge | n | entry | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no rebound) | 196 | +55.1 bps | 54% | +1.09 |
| **0.80** (real planted rebound) | 142 | +542.5 bps | 84% | **+9.65** |

With no planted rebound the control sits near *t* ≈ 0 (averaged over seeds, mean *t* ≈ 0.55 — the
+1.09 here is ordinary sampling scatter, not a biased detector); a real planted rebound lights up
at *t* = +9.65 with an 84% win-rate. The detector is live and unbiased.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The DeMarker oversold-rising entry beats a drift-matched random baseline by a
  positive margin at every horizon, and the difference **clears Welch *t* ≥ 2 at one of four
  horizons** (20-day *t* = +2.61, *p* = 0.009). But it is not robust: 5/10/60-day never reach 2,
  and the 20-day significance is carried almost entirely by IWM (drop it → *t* = 1.40). More than
  the usual mirage, far short of a clean edge.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The only significant horizon hangs on a single instrument and a
  single hold; positive deltas survive costs (the entry is in-sample), but there is no robust,
  scalable edge here — you would be betting on one ticker's quirk at one horizon.
- **"Does the DeMarker forecast exhaustion turns?" — MIXED.** The phase-scramble placebo says the
  timing is *marginally* load-bearing (*p* = 0.044), and every ticker's delta is positive — so this
  is not the flat "geometric nonsense does just as well" of a busted indicator. But the
  significance is single-horizon and single-ticker fragile, so the exhaustion-turn claim is neither
  confirmed nor cleanly busted: it is mixed.
